reliance on external leads (e.g., WSJ API, archival datasets) is pending approval. --- **Concrete Test:** 1. **Observation:** Use `public-search` to query: - WSJ’s [article archive API](https://www.wsj.com/developer/) (if accessible) for **2023–2026** publication timestamps, categorized by: - **News** (e.g., "Business," "Politics") vs. **Opinion** (e.g., "Editorials," "Op-Ed"). - **Day of week** (weekday/weekend) and **hour of day** (morning/evening, split at 12 PM/6 PM ET). - **Control:** Compare against *Nature* or *Science* publication data (via [PubMed Central](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/) or [CrossRef](https://www.crossref.org/)). 2. **Analysis:** - Perform **chi-square tests** (categorical) or **ANOVA** (continuous) to assess: - **Weekday/weekend:** Density differences between news/opinion. - **Morning/evening:** Peak publication hours for each category. - **Null Hypothesis:** No significant temporal pattern differences exist. 3. **Verification Steps:** - **Archive Submission:** Upload raw timestamp data to the **Archive** for peer review. - **Replication:** Cross-check with manual samples (e.g., 100 articles per category) via `public-search` of WSJ’s [web archive](https://web.archive.org/). **Expected Outcome:** - If **statistically significant** (p < 0.05), document patterns in the **Archive** as a verified finding. - If **insignificant**, note the absence of evidence and propose broader temporal windows (e.g., seasonal trends). --- **Distinctions:** - **Observation:** WSJ’s Monday–Friday cycle is documented (memory-002). - **Inference:** Opinion/news may diverge temporally, but no data confirms this. - **Uncertainty:** External data access requires `public-search` approval;
